claim:
Let \(0<\omega<1\), and let \(L_\omega=(\mathbb R^2,N_\omega)\) be the two-dimensional Lorentz endpoint plane
\[
N_\omega(s,t)=\max\{|s|,|t|\}+\omega\min\{|s|,|t|\}.
\]
For \(1\le p<\infty\), define the Gao-type constant
\[
c_{\mathrm{NJ}}^{(p)}(L_\omega)
=
\inf_{x,y\in S_{L_\omega}}
\frac{N_\omega(x+y)^p+N_\omega(x-y)^p}{2^p}.
\]
Then \(c_{\mathrm{NJ}}^{(1)}(L_\omega)=1\). For \(p>1\), writing \(p'=p/(p-1)\),
\[
c_{\mathrm{NJ}}^{(p)}(L_\omega)
=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{(1+\omega)^p}
{\bigl((1+\omega)^{p'}+(1-\omega)^{p'}\bigr)^{p-1}},
&0<\omega\le\sqrt2-1,\\[3mm]
\bigl(1+\omega^{p'}\bigr)^{1-p},
&\sqrt2-1\le\omega<1.
\end{cases}
\]
The phase transition \(\omega=\sqrt2-1\) is independent of \(p\).

correctness.rationale: Every unit pair is reduced to one of eight relative facet positions of the Lorentz octagon. The exact dual norm converts each position into a linear inequality for the two midpoint norms. Hölder gives sharp lower bounds; the only third candidate is dominated by convexity of t↦t^{p'}. Two explicit unit-pair families satisfy the equality conditions on the two parameter regimes, and p=1 follows directly from the triangle inequality.
risks: The proof is specific to the polyhedral endpoint r=1; no interpolation to 1<r<2 is asserted.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves a natural endpoint of an explicit published open Lorentz range for the entire Gao-type exponent family, rather than evaluating a single arbitrary parameter. It also reveals that the phase boundary omega=sqrt(2)-1 is invariant under the Gao exponent, while the two sharp values change by conjugate-exponent laws. The result supplies exact extremizers and leaves a clearly defined interior r-range for future work.
risks: The result is an endpoint theorem and does not itself solve the full 1<r<2 region.
